bleeding.title: Stay calm and call for help immediately
Apply firm pressure on the wound using a cloth or clothing
bleeding.detail: Do not remove the cloth if it soaks through — add more on top

bleeding.title: Elevate the injured limb above heart level if possible
Keep the person warm and still
bleeding.detail: Do not offer food or water

fracture.title: Do not try to straighten the bone
fracture.detail: Moving it causes more damage to nerves and blood vessels

fracture.title: Immobilise the area using splints or rolled clothing
fracture.detail: Pad the splint with cloth to reduce pressure

fracture.title: Apply an ice pack wrapped in cloth to reduce swelling
fracture.detail: Never apply ice directly to skin

fracture.title: Keep the person still and comfortable
fracture.detail: Do not offer food or water in case surgery is needed

unconscious.title: Check if the person is breathing — look, listen, feel
unconscious.detail: Tilt head back slightly and look for chest rise

unconscious.title: Place in recovery position if breathing
unconscious.detail: This prevents choking if they vomit

unconscious.title: Begin CPR if not breathing — 30 compressions, 2 rescue breaths
unconscious.detail: Push hard and fast at 100–120 compressions per minute

unconscious.title: Do not give water or food; keep them warm

burns.title: Remove the person from the source of heat immediately
Cool the burn with cool (not cold) running water for 10–20 minutes
burns.detail: Never use ice, butter, or toothpaste on burns

burns.title: Remove jewellery or tight clothing near the burn
Cover loosely with a clean non-fluffy material
burns.detail: Use cling film or a clean plastic bag if available

burns.title: Call emergency services for large or deep burns

choking.title: Ask the person if they can speak or cough
choking.detail: If they can, encourage them to keep coughing

choking.title: Give up to 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades
choking.detail: Use the heel of your hand

choking.title: Give up to 5 abdominal thrusts (Heimlich manoeuvre)
choking.detail: Stand behind them, make a fist above the navel, pull sharply inward and upward

choking.title: Alternate between 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts
choking.detail: Stop if the object is expelled

choking.title: Call emergency services if the obstruction does not clear

heart_attack.title: Have the person sit or lie down in a comfortable position
If they are conscious and not allergic, give aspirin to chew
heart_attack.detail: 325mg if available — do not swallow whole

heart_attack.title: Begin CPR if they become unconscious and stop breathing

seizure.title: Stay calm and time the seizure
Clear the area of hard or sharp objects
Place something soft under their head
Turn them gently on their side after convulsions stop
Do not put anything in their mouth
Call emergency services if seizure lasts more than 5 minutes

drowning.title: Remove the person from water safely — do not put yourself at risk
drowning.detail: Use a rope, branch or flotation device if possible

drowning.title: Check for breathing — tilt head back and lift chin
Give 5 rescue breaths if not breathing
Begin CPR — 30 compressions, 2 breaths
drowning.detail: Continue until help arrives or person recovers
